column1: # The golden first adoption (SET-11), recorded 2026-11-11 on a second machine: native Windows, several repos, one operation session.
# Setup replays these in order, compares each observed result with the golden one and stops at the first mismatch, asking for the fix.

column3: git, python3 and gh installed; gh auth status shows the owner signed in; no fcntl or getuid crash; the qa lane runs on the adopter's platform (on the first run it hung on os.getuid)
column4: install the missing tool; gh auth login with a device code relayed to the owner; update to a release with the platform fix

column3: the chosen repos, picked from gh repo list by last push with private ones included, are cloned into one folder and registered with board.py repos add; repos list shows exactly that set
column4: clone the missing repo into the folder and run board.py repos add, or remove the one not chosen

column3: skills are linked as real symlinks; ~/.workflow-loop/flow.json is filled; ~/.workflow-loop/private-names holds at least one pattern and private.py check says on
column4: rerun the install with real symlinks (on Windows, MSYS=winsymlinks:nativestrict); fill flow.json; add a pattern to private-names

column3: update --apply is merged in every followed repo; the board shows no repo with template version unknown
column4: run update --apply in that repo and merge its update branch

column3: the reply hook and the govern hook are each installed exactly once in the operation repo machine-local Claude settings
column4: run reply-hook once; remove the duplicate entry

column3: each connector a followed repo PRDs need is probed read-only and printed connected, needs sign-in or missing
column4: the owner attaches or signs in to that connector with the narrowest access

column3: every queued goal is bound to an app session before operate starts; no background worker runs; pool.py need follows its rule (0 when no goal waits)
column4: start a session for the goal and bind it; stop the background worker; set session_command

column3: operate.py run is started and its first check-in has exactly five parts: headline, All sessions table, a Dependencies graph per followed repo with its legend, Needs you, Coming up; the reply hook passes it
column4: start operate.py run; fix the check-in to the five-part layout
